The package extracts an AppImage during packaging, inspects its contents to detect the Electron version, and adjusts scripts and desktop files accordingly. While this is somewhat unusual, it is not inherently malicious. The script modifies the AppImage's desktop file and wrapper script using `sed`, replacing placeholders with correct values such as the package name and Electron version. It also replaces the bundled `7za` binary with a symlink to the system's `/usr/bin/7za`, improving maintainability and security by relying on the system package.

No network requests are made during build or install, no code is downloaded and executed dynamically (e.g., `curl | bash`), and no obfuscation is present. All operations are transparent, focused on repackaging an upstream AppImage into a native Arch Linux package. The maintainer includes informative warnings about Electron version mismatches, suggesting a focus on usability and correctness rather than stealthy exploitation. The package does not access or exfiltrate sensitive data, nor does it modify system configuration outside the package directory.
</details>
